newsitem.title: USA: U.S. help-wanted ad index fell to 82 in October.
newsitem.headline: U.S. help-wanted ad index fell to 82 in October.

text.p: The U.S. help-wanted advertising index slipped two points to 82.0 in October, the Conference Board said on Wednesday.

In the last three months, the volume of help-wanted advertising rose in five of the nine U.S. regions. The greatest increase was in New England, followed by the Pacific, Mountain and South Atlantic regions. The East North Central region posted the biggest decline.
"The labor market is not slowing down in the fourth quarter," Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein said in a statement.

"The pace of jobs growth will not subside in the early months of 1997," he added. "Sustained job growth will bolster consumer confidence and lead to strong consumer spending through the first half of the year."
